eyebrow: Docker & Deployment for AI Applications · Chapter Two
subtitle: Lesson 9 · Containerizing AI Applications

eyebrow: ENV vs. -e: baked in, or supplied at startup
code:
# Dockerfile - baked in, same for every container
ENV LOG_LEVEL=info

# docker run - per-container, never part of the image
docker run -e OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... my-ai-app:1.0
caption: Secrets go in as -e at runtime, never as ENV in the Dockerfile.

eyebrow: Why a RUN with a secret is a trap
code:
# WRONG: the key is now permanently in this layer's history
RUN echo "sk-abc123" > /tmp/key.txt && \
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /tmp/key.txt)" ...
RUN rm /tmp/key.txt   # does NOT remove it from the layer above
caption: A later RUN rm hides a file. It does not erase it from the image's history.

eyebrow: --env-file for more than a few variables
code:
# .env.production (never committed to git)
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
DATABASE_URL=postgres://...

docker run --env-file .env.production my-ai-app:1.0
caption: Same effect as many -e flags, read from a file that belongs in .gitignore.

code:
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=pip_token \
  pip install --index-url https://$(cat /run/secrets/pip_token)@pypi.example.com

docker build --secret id=pip_token,src=./pip_token.txt -t my-ai-app .
caption: Available only for one RUN instruction — never written into any layer.
